key_insight: Data reuploading expands a quantum circuit’s accessible Fourier spectrum in a precisely characterizable way, but its representational capacity grows only polynomially with reuploads and depends strongly on the encoding spectrum.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical rule for designing quantum neural networks: more reuploads increase expressivity, yet scaling benefits are limited and must be balanced against parameterization, input encoding, and task dimensionality.
method: Characterize the QDR frequency set as the R-fold sumset of encoding differences, with an exact word-length criterion in an integer lattice.
Prove that spectrum directions stabilize at one reupload, while frequency magnitude and count grow with R.
Use the spectrum size to derive a Rademacher-complexity capacity bound for QDRs.
evidence_signal: Experiments on function approximation and classification matched the spectral theory exactly and showed a single-qubit QDR can outperform a matched MLP on some smooth/periodic and low-dimensional tasks, but not on higher-dimensional regression.
watch_item: Performance is highly sensitive to the input-encoding scale and degrades on multivariate problems, so reupload depth alone is not a reliable indicator of generalization.
paper_title: On the Expressive Power and Capacity of Quantum Data Reuploaders
